title: Topological edge and domain-wall phonons in the mass-dimerized diatomic chain: complex band structure, Zak phase, and spectral unfolding
abstract: The one-dimensional chain with alternating masses is the simplest mechanical system with a topological band structure. We give a fully analytical account of its localized vibrations built on the complex band structure. The evanescent Bloch waves available at each frequency are matched directly to force balance at a free end or a domain wall, without transfer matrices, which yields closed-form frequencies and decay lengths for every localized mode. The free-end mode sits at a branch point of the complex band structure, where the acoustic and optical sheets join and the decay is fastest. For uniform springs, a sharp wall between the two mass orderings hosts one in-gap mode, symmetric at the light$\mid$light wall and antisymmetric at the heavy$\mid$heavy wall, and an adiabatic construction shows that these are the same topological mode; the light$\mid$light wall also binds a non-topological mode above the optical branch. Spectral unfolding makes this classification visible in momentum space: the sign of the Bloch factor sets the zone-center or zone-boundary character of each mode, and its magnitude sets the width. The Zak phase, quantized by inversion, identifies the modes of topological origin and fixes a half-integer mode count per band at a wall, while the chiral symmetry known to be hidden in strain coordinates explains which frequencies are pinned.
summary: This paper analytically investigates the vibrational modes of a mass-dimerized diatomic chain, treating it as a phononic analogue to topological insulators. By analyzing the complex band structure and calculating the Zak phase, the authors rigorously classify localized modes at free ends and domain walls. This work establishes a clear link between bulk topology and the existence of gap states in mechanical systems.
main_problem: To provide a unified analytical treatment for the bulk topology, complex band structure, and the full spectrum of localized modes (edge and domain-wall) in a mass-dimerized diatomic chain.
main_result: The analysis yields closed-form frequencies and decay lengths for all localized modes, distinguishing between modes protected by bulk topology (via the Zak phase) and those set by local geometry.
method: The authors use complex band structure analysis, matching evanescent Bloch waves directly to force balance conditions at boundaries, and employing the Zak phase to quantify topological invariants.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional diatomic chain with alternating masses (mass-dimerized), modeled as an SSH-type phononic system where dimerization is introduced via mass contrast.
key_observables: Phonon dispersion relation ($\omega^2_{\pm}(q)$), Zak phase ($\gamma_{\pm}$), Wannier center position, and localized mode frequencies.
important_parameters: Mass ratio ($m_2/m_1$), spring constant ($K$), and the dimerization strength ($\delta$ or $\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the validity of matching evanescent Bloch waves to force balance conditions and assumes the presence of inversion symmetry for Zak phase quantization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phonon band structure for varying mass ratios and show the localized antisymmetric states at domain walls (H|H and L|L) as a function of interfacial spring strength ($\lambda$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the general dispersion relation to analyzing the topological invariants (Zak phase) that characterize the bulk, and finally contrasts symmetry-protected modes with topologically-protected modes at interfaces.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of topological invariants (Zak phase) to mechanical lattice vibrations provides a powerful analogy to electronic band theory, offering new insights into how geometry dictates vibrational modes.
